correctness.rationale: Direct Gaussian radial integration diagonalizes the true order-two Hermite basis. Exact adjacent-eigenvalue identity is proved algebraically. The nonstandard global comparison uses the strict right-shift inequality f_n(n+s)>f_n(n-s) and its Gamma median corollary λ_n(n)<1/2, then finite analytic endpoint comparisons. This determines the maximum and next distinct eigenspaces for all x>0, including integer resonances. Orthogonal spectral decomposition gives a sharp quantitative gap. 542 exact-rational assertions reproduced from packaged verify.py; not used as a proof of infinitely many indices.

originality.rationale: Full Sections 4–5 of the 2018 Hermite-window large-sieve source and Section 6 of the 2019 radial polyanalytic spectral paper were compared at statement/implication level. Both provide eigenvalue machinery but neither reports the all-radius leading/second eigenindex classification, three-dimensional critical maximum, or the sharp stability law. The Gaussian-window and other published-finding corpus spectral findings have different objects; the old exact integral alone does not supply the new global comparison and gap. No matching new result was found in the accessible prior ledgers. Residual literature incompleteness acknowledged; priority not independently certified.
residual_risks: Earlier specialized literature on Laguerre-weighted disk localization or first-Hermite spectrograms could state an equivalent all-radius spectral ordering and gap in different terminology.
The full 1988 original Daubechies paper was not retrieved; available summaries and subsequent use concern the Gaussian analysis window.
A semantic database search is not a mathematical uniqueness proof; independent historical priority review remains necessary.

value.rationale: First excited Hermite-window disk concentration is a natural fixed-window sharp time-frequency localization question highlighted by 2018 Hermite large-sieve work. Its global spectral ordering is qualitatively different from Gaussian-window disk concentration: a real transition from excited to ground input mode, a threefold critical maximizing eigenspace, and the exact radius-dependent gap including an additional runner-up resonance. Explicit optimal quantitative stability is valuable for robust reconstruction and is not a mere numerical restatement of a known eigenvalue integral. Scope is one natural lowest non-Gaussian Landau level, not an arbitrary small slice.
